{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex, by email, relayed by Anthony 2026-09-17, in his words: "Repo nav know-how is per-project, per-repo procedural knowledge. reflow2 does no file I/O by design. The agent is storing information about how to navigate the repos." "After upgrade, these are thin project adapters, not competing playbooks." He asks for "a first-class way to teach the agent a repo's import/resolver/test conventions."

═══ WHAT THE DESIGN ALREADY HOLDS ═══
· dec:skills-served (accepted, his own 2026-07-25 idea) — its option (4) LOCAL OVERRIDE: "a skill present in the project's own .claude/skills/ wins over the served one, so customisation survives and the served set is a default rather than a cage." The adapter is that override, seen from the project side.
· dec:idea-a-principle-has-a-universal-core-and-local-clothes, option C — the served core with a project-local instantiation slot; the same figure for principles.
· DesignRule with `category: convention` and `steps` — a convention the project follows, delivered at the step it concerns. "Imports resolve through X; tests run with Y" is a convention in exactly that sense, and get_skill already carries rules naming that skill beside it.
· AGENTS.md — the file every agent reads before it knows reflow2 exists, and where this repo's own build conventions live; a consumer's AGENTS.md is the same slot.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══
A. ⭐ THE ADAPTER IS A DESIGN RULE WITH STEPS, and the design knows it. A repo's conventions land as DesignRules of category `convention` whose `steps` name the served skills they bear on (adopt, link-artifacts, root-cause), so get_skill delivers them beside the skill — no project-local skill file needed for the know-how half, and the design can say what conventions a project follows. Cheap; the vocabulary exists. ⚠️ Counter: a rule is a sentence and repo navigation is often a procedure; the `steps` field delivers, it does not execute.
B. A PROJECT-LOCAL SKILL, ACKNOWLEDGED: keep the thin adapter as a .claude/skills file, and register it as an Artifact that DOCUMENTS the Project with doc_kind `agent_instructions`, so the design knows the adapter exists and reconcile notices when it drifts. The override already wins; this only makes it visible.
C. A `conventions` PROPERTY ON PROJECT — import root, resolver, test command — read by nothing. ⚠️ The declared-field-nobody-reads trap.
D. NOTHING: AGENTS.md already is the adapter. ⚠️ Counter: it is a file nobody in the graph points at, so it is a document in exactly the sense the design refuses to keep design information in.

═══ THE HONEST LIMIT ═══
